Flask

Flask is a lightweight Python web framework used to build web applications, REST APIs, dashboards, automation tools, and backend services. Xenors provides Flask tutorials, practical examples, deployment guides, database integration, authentication, and API development resources.

Learn Flask routing, Jinja templates, SQLAlchemy, SQLite, MySQL, REST APIs, authentication, file uploads, deployment, and modern Python backend development.

When Flask Is a Good Choice

Flask gives developers a small core and freedom to choose the database, authentication approach and project structure that fit the application. It is well suited to REST APIs, lightweight dashboards, automation interfaces and services where a full framework would add unnecessary complexity.

That flexibility also means production concerns must be designed deliberately. Use an application factory or organized package structure as the codebase grows, keep secrets in environment variables, validate inputs and run behind a production WSGI server or appropriate hosting platform. SQLAlchemy, migrations and tested authentication patterns are common additions for data-driven applications.

How to use this section

Flask is a lightweight Python web framework that is useful for APIs, small web applications and learning how HTTP request handling works. Its minimal core makes routing, templates, configuration and extensions visible instead of hiding them behind a large framework.

A good Flask project separates configuration, routes, business logic and data access as it grows. Start simple, but avoid putting every feature into one file once the application has several routes or external dependencies.

Security matters from the first deployment: validate input, protect secrets, configure sessions correctly and use a production server rather than Flask's development server for public traffic.
